transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I’ve been having thoughts like… maybe my family would be better off if I just didn’t wake up. That scared me. I told my supervisor, and they said I should come in and talk to someone.
When did you start having these thoughts about your family being better off without you?
It started recently enough that it scared me. I kept thinking my family might be better off if I just didn’t wake up, and that’s when I told my supervisor I needed help.
How many days or weeks have you been having these thoughts about your family being better off without you?
About two weeks. It kind of started after my daughter left Georgia for the military, and since then this whole change in me has been going on.
Have you been feeling sad or empty most of the time since your daughter left for the military?
I’m not really sure how to describe it. I know I haven’t felt right since she left, but I don’t know if I’d say sad or empty most of the time. It’s just been… different, heavier.
Have you been enjoying activities that you normally like to do since your daughter left for the military?

No, not really. I used to mess with my tomato plants, work on sanding wood out at my bench, watch the Falcons, stay around after church and talk with folks. Lately I just look at all that like it belongs to somebody else. I don’t really feel like doing any of it.
Have you noticed any change in your weight since your daughter left for the military?

I haven’t really weighed myself, so I can’t say for sure. But my appetite’s been off. Most days I have to make myself eat a few bites, and even stuff I usually like just sits there until I end up throwing it out.
Have you been feeling restless or slowed down since your daughter left for the military?
Yeah… more slowed down than restless. Folks at work keep asking me if I’m sick. I’m walking slower, and it takes me too long to answer simple questions. It’s like my body’s moving through mud.
Have you been feeling guilty about anything since your daughter left for the military?

Yeah… I have. I keep thinking about her leaving and telling myself I must’ve done something wrong as her dad. Like if I’d been better, maybe I would’ve handled things different, or she wouldn’t have felt like she had to go. I know that may not make sense, but that’s where my mind keeps going.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy doing since your daughter left for the military?

Not really, no. I used to mess with my tomato plants, work on sanding wood at my bench, watch the Falcons, and stay after church talking with folks. Lately I just look at all that like it belongs to somebody else. I don’t get much out of it.
Have you had any days in the past two weeks where you felt somewhat better, or has it been consistently difficult the whole time?

It’s been pretty steady difficult the whole time. This change in me started around when my daughter left Georgia for the military, and it’s been about two weeks now. I can’t really point to a good day in there.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy, but now find pleasure in only slightly, since your daughter left for the military?

Yeah… those same things. I can still sit out by the tomato plants or go to my workbench, maybe turn on the Falcons, but it’s only a little bit there, if anything. Even staying after church talking with people doesn’t feel like it used to. It’s like I’m doing it, but it doesn’t really feel like mine anymore.
Have you had any thoughts of suicide besides thinking your family would be better off without you?
No… not beyond that, really. It’s mostly that thought that maybe they’d be better off if I just didn’t wake up. It scared me enough that I told my supervisor, and that’s why I came in.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in since your daughter left for the military?

Not much, no. I used to mess with my tomato plants, sand wood at my bench, watch the Falcons, stay after church and talk… but lately I just kind of look at all that like it belongs to somebody else. I don’t really get much pleasure from it.
Have you been experiencing these thoughts and feelings almost every day since your daughter left for the military?
Yes… pretty much every day. It’s been about two weeks now, since my daughter left Georgia for the military, and this whole change in me has just been hanging around.
Have you been experiencing significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning since your daughter left for the military?

Yes. It’s been affecting things pretty bad. At work I started making mistakes, and it got serious enough that my supervisor found me sitting in my truck before dawn and got occupational health involved. And at home, I’ve let bills and other responsibilities pile up instead of taking care of them like I normally would.
Would you say these feelings and thoughts have been mild, moderate, or severe for you over the past two weeks?
I’d say moderate. It’s been more than just a little sadness, but I don’t know that I’d call it the worst it could be. It’s definitely been weighing on me and getting in the way.
